source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Ousmane Dieng
injuries.short_comment: Dieng (finger) is questionable for Monday's game against the Raptors.
injuries.long_comment: Dieng has missed the last four games while recovering from a procedure to repair a fractured left finger. He reportedly underwent surgery Nov. 16, so his questionable status is somewhat shocking considering it's only been one week. Still, Milwaukee will provide another update prior to tip.

injuries.name: RJ Barrett
injuries.short_comment: Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

injuries.name: Nate Bittle
injuries.short_comment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injuries.long_comment: Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

injuries.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
injuries.short_comment: Murray-Boyles (concussion) is listed as probable for Monday's game against Milwaukee, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injuries.long_comment: Murray-Boyles exited Wednesday's game versus the Wizards and didn't suit up for Friday's 105-102 win over the Pistons. It appears a one-game absence will be all that is needed for the 21-year-old, though it's unclear if he will reclaim his spot in the starting lineup over Allen Graves.

injuries.name: Kawhi Leonard
injuries.short_comment: Leonard (knee) could return in the next few weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long_comment: This was the expectation after the Raptors ruled out the star forward Tuesday for at least one more week. Collin Murray-Boyles should continue to handle a larger role once he passes the concussion protocol, and Ja'Kobe Walter should remain a starter for the time being.
